terms.meaning: a piece of the page that runs in the browser and handles clicks and typing
a browser box asking the user to confirm before an action runs

used_by: src/app/crews/[crewId] page (exact link not in the packet)

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for crew controls
sections.what: Loads the router and the state hook, and marks the file as running in the browser.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the controls needing browser behaviour.

sections.name: call
sections.title: Request helper for crew actions
sections.what: Sends a POST or DELETE to an address, and returns a success flag and any data, treating an empty response as empty data.
sections.why: Likely reason: one shared way to send requests keeps error handling the same everywhere.
sections.watch_out: If a response is not JSON, the data quietly becomes empty and the message falls back to generic text.

sections.name: InvitePanel
sections.title: Invite code and link panel
sections.what: Shows the invite code and a link, with a copy button, and lets the owner make a new code that replaces the old one.
sections.why: Likely reason: owners need a way to cancel invites that have leaked.
sections.watch_out: A new code cancels all old invite links immediately, so an accidental click breaks shared invites.

sections.name: RemoveMemberButton
sections.title: Remove member button
sections.what: Asks for confirmation, then asks the server to remove the member and refreshes the page. Shows an alert if removal fails.
sections.why: Likely reason: the confirmation prevents accidental removal.
sections.watch_out: The confirmation is only a click check, so the server must refuse non-owners.

sections.name: LeaveButton
sections.title: Leave crew button
sections.what: Asks for confirmation, then asks the server to leave the crew and sends the member to the crews list. Shows any error below the button.
sections.why: Likely reason: the confirmation prevents accidental leaving.
sections.watch_out: What happens to ownership when the owner leaves is decided on the server and is not visible here.

sections.name: send
sections.title: Request helper with a body
sections.what: Sends a request with an optional JSON body and returns a success flag, or the server's message if it fails.
sections.why: Likely reason: report and block need to send data, which the other helper does not do.
sections.watch_out: This duplicates the logic of the other helper with a different result shape, so changes must be made in both places.

sections.name: MemberMenu
sections.title: Member options menu
sections.what: Offers a report with a reason choice, a block with confirmation, and for owners a make-owner action. Shows the result in a note.
sections.why: Likely reason: any member can report or block, and only the owner can hand over the crew.
sections.watch_out: The reason choices are fixed in the page, so a new reason must be added here and on the server.

sections.name: ResolveReportButton
sections.title: Mark report resolved button
sections.what: Asks the server to mark a report resolved and refreshes the page when it works.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond matching the resolve action.
sections.watch_out: A failure gives no message at all, so the owner may think the report was resolved when it was not.

summary: The client-side controls on a crew's page: invite code and link, leave, remove members, the per-member options menu, and resolving reports.
purpose: Gives members and owners the actions they need to manage a crew from the page.
why: The file splits each control into its own piece so owner-only actions can be shown or hidden.
how: Each control sends a request to a crew route, then refreshes the page or shows a message. Owner-only controls are shown only when the owner flag is true.
inputs: Crew id, user ids, names and owner flags passed in by the crew page.
outputs: Buttons, forms, confirmation dialogs, and short messages on the page.
risks: Several actions rely on browser confirmation boxes, and the real permission checks live on the server.
debug: If a button does nothing, check the matching route and the response it returns. If a message is missing, check the failure path in that control.
